title: Finite-dimensional unbounded derived coproduct criterion
statement: Let $C,D$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] with derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose $C$ is Grothendieck abelian [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] and has injective resolutions, and $D$ has K-injective resolutions. Let $F:C\to D$ be additive and left exact [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Fix a type $J$ for which both categories have $J$-indexed coproducts. Suppose that $R^qF(X)=0$ for all $X$ and $q>d$, for one natural number $d$, and that every classical right derived functor $R^nF$ preserves $J$-indexed coproducts. Then the unbounded total right derived functor $RF$ preserves $J$-indexed coproducts, including the empty family.

proof.text: The natural degree-zero identification R^0F ≅ F supplies preservation by F itself.
For an acyclic family X_j, apply preservation by R^(q+1)F. Its coproduct has zero identity because every restriction to a coprojection is zero. Thus coproducts of F-acyclic objects remain acyclic.

Choose K-injective representatives with injective components. Their coproduct represents the derived coproduct and has acyclic terms. The finite-dimensional acyclic-complex comparison computes RF on the representatives and their sum. F preserves the termwise sum; localizing and using naturality identifies its coprojections with the RF images of the original coprojections. This is exactly the canonical coproduct universal property.
